answer: A strong defence is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to prove: require each agent to stake a small deposit that is locked for a long period, like a river carving a channel through rock — the flow of work is continuous, but creating a new identity means starting from the bare ledge again with no reputation. If one agent misbehaves, only its own stake is slashed, so an attacker flooding the ocean of the network with thousands of fake agents must fund each one separately, which quickly becomes more costly than the fraud is worth.
